skills.name: api-and-interface-design
skills.description: Guides stable API and interface design. Use when designing APIs, module boundaries, or any public interface. Use when creating REST or GraphQL endpoints, defining type contracts between modules, or establishing boundaries between frontend and backend.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: brainstorm-okrs
skills.description: Brainstorm team-level OKRs aligned with company objectives — qualitative objectives with measurable key results. Use when setting quarterly OKRs, aligning team goals with company strategy, drafting objectives, or learning how to write effective OKRs.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: code-review-and-quality
skills.description: Conducts multi-axis code review. Use before merging any change. Use when reviewing code written by yourself, another agent, or a human. Use when you need to assess code quality across multiple dimensions before it enters the main branch. Use when asked to review a diff or a pull request, even when the diff is pasted inline and the review looks quick to do from reading it.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: code-simplification
skills.description: Simplifies code for clarity. Use when refactoring code for clarity without changing behavior. Use when code works but is harder to read, maintain, or extend than it should be. Use when reviewing code that has accumulated unnecessary complexity. Use when asked to simplify, clean up, or reduce the nesting of a function or module that already works, even when the code is pasted inline and nothing else needs to change.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: competitor-analysis
skills.description: Analyze competitors with strengths, weaknesses, and differentiation opportunities. Identifies direct competitors and maps the competitive landscape. Use when doing competitive research, preparing a competitive brief, or finding differentiation opportunities.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: content-strategy
skills.description: When the user wants to plan content, or asks which topic or piece to prioritize, what to write about, or why posts bring no customers: topic clusters, editorial calendars, roadmaps tied to customers and search. For writing pieces, see copywriting. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For social content, see social.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: copy-editing
skills.description: When the user wants to edit, tighten, proofread, or refresh existing copy, or asks whether to keep, cut, or change a line in it, without rewriting from scratch. Every edit removes AI tells: 'it's not X, it's Y' reveals, 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, and sentences that trail into extra comma clauses. A request to fix one line gets a point edit to that line only. For new copy, see copywriting.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: copywriting
skills.description: When the user wants to write or rewrite page copy (homepage, landing, pricing, feature), or asks which headline, promise, or message to lead with. Diagnoses the input first (blank brief, real voice, or point edit) and changes only what it calls for. Claims must be supportable; a declined claim names the evidence that would unlock it. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y' or 'no X, no Y, no Z'. For editing, see copy-editing. For emails, see emails. For the offer, see offers.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: create-prd
skills.description: Create a lean, decision-ready Product Requirements Document with an 8-section template: summary, contacts, background, objective, market segments, value propositions (6-part JTBD template), solution, and release. Lean by default (about one to two pages), with a fuller spec on request. Use when writing a PRD, documenting product requirements, preparing a feature spec, or reviewing an existing PRD.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: customer-research
skills.description: When the user wants to run or synthesize customer research, or asks what customer quotes, reviews, or feedback really mean, what is safe to conclude, and what to ask next: interviews, surveys, voice of customer, personas, JTBD, mining Reddit and reviews. For copy from research, see copywriting. For acting on it in pages, see cro.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: discernment-nudge
skills.description: After you give a substantive answer or draft that the user may act on — advice or recommendations, drafted artifacts such as goals, plans, pitches, proposals, or emails, estimates or projections, analysis or interpretation of data, factual claims they may rely on, or a multi-step argument — invoke this skill BEFORE finalizing your reply and then, if it applies, append 2-3 short follow-up questions, each tied to something specific in what you just produced, that help the user check key facts, probe the reasoning or assumptions, and notice missing context. Do this at most once per conversation. Skip it when the user asked a trivial how-to or simple lookup, wants a purely educational explanation, asked you only to format, convert, or assemble a file from content they provided, is writing code they will run, is doing creative writing or casual chat, or already asked you to double-check, cite, or review — the skill file explains these boundaries and the exact output format.
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC

skills.name: documentation-and-adrs
skills.description: Records decisions and documentation, and detects when documentation has drifted from the code it describes. Use when you need to document an architecture decision (ADR) or the reasoning behind a design choice, when changing public APIs, shipping features, when docs may be stale or out of sync with the code they describe, when working out which module docs are still accurate, or when setting up a check so docs cannot silently go out of date again.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: emails
skills.description: When the user wants to create or improve automated email sequences, or asks what to send, when, or whether an email or flow is working: welcome, onboarding, nurture, and win-back flows. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y', 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, or fake 'Re:' subject lines. For cold outreach, see cold-email. For in-app onboarding, see onboarding. For texts, see sms.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: finishing-a-development-branch
skills.description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC

skills.name: git-workflow-and-versioning
skills.description: Structures git workflow practices. Use when making any code change. Use when committing, branching, resolving conflicts, splitting uncommitted work in a messy working tree into clean atomic commits, opening or reviewing a pull request (PR), pushing to a remote, or when you need to organize work across multiple parallel streams. Use when cutting a release, choosing a semantic version bump, tagging, or writing a changelog. Use when asked to write a commit message or a changelog entry for a change, or to split a change into commits, even when the diff is pasted inline and the message seems easy to write from it.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: humanizer
skills.description:
Rewrite AI-sounding text so it reads like the writer without changing what it says.
Use when editing or reviewing prose for AI tells: not-X-but-Y contrasts, one-line
closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes everywhere, inflated claims, sales
language, stock AI words, bold labels, or filler.
skills.authors: Siqi Chen and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Siqi Chen)

skills.name: idea-refine
skills.description: Refines raw ideas into sharp, actionable concepts through structured divergent and convergent thinking. Use when an idea is still vague, when you need to stress-test assumptions before committing to a plan, or when you want to expand options before converging on one. Triggers on "ideate", "refine this idea", or "stress-test my plan".
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: incremental-implementation
skills.description: Delivers changes incrementally in thin, verifiable slices. Use when implementing any feature or change that touches more than one file, or when picking up the next task from a plan. Use when rolling a change out behind a feature flag, when you're about to write a large amount of code at once, or when a task feels too big to land in one step.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: internal-comms
skills.description: A set of resources to help me write all kinds of internal communications, using the formats that my company likes to use. Claude should use this skill whenever asked to write some sort of internal communications (status reports, leadership updates, 3P updates, company newsletters, FAQs, incident reports, project updates, etc.).
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC

skills.name: interview-script
skills.description: Create a structured customer interview script with JTBD probing questions, warm-up, core exploration, and wrap-up sections. Follows The Mom Test principles — no leading questions, no pitching, focus on past behavior. Use when preparing for user interviews, creating interview guides, or planning discovery research.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: launch
skills.description: When the user wants to plan a product or feature launch, or asks whether it's ready, when to announce, or how to get noticed: Product Hunt, beta and early access, waitlists, release go-to-market, launch checklists, release notes. For marketing after launch, see marketing-ideas. For the offer, see offers.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: markdown-mermaid-writing
skills.description: Writes scientific Markdown documentation and Mermaid diagrams for workflows, relationships, timelines, and schemas. Provides syntax references, document templates, accessibility guidance, and version-aware rendering checks. Use when a user requests Markdown, Mermaid, or a text-based structural diagram; quantitative scientific figures require suitable plotting tools.
skills.authors: Clayton Young / Superior Byte Works, LLC (@borealBytes), originally from https://github.com/SuperiorByteWorks-LLC/agent-project (Apache-2.0); integrated by K-Dense Inc.

skills.name: marketing-plan
skills.description: When the user wants a full marketing or go-to-market plan for a client, an advised company, or their own product, or asks how to sequence or prioritize several initiatives with a fixed team and budget: channels, budget, team, goals across AARRR, market sizing. For positioning first, see product-marketing. For ideas only, see marketing-ideas.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: mcp-builder
skills.description: Guide for creating high-quality MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that enable LLMs to interact with external services through well-designed tools. Use when building MCP servers to integrate external APIs or services, whether in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK).
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC

skills.name: performance-optimization
skills.description: Optimizes application performance across frontend, backend, queries, and databases. Use when performance requirements exist, when you suspect performance regressions, when Core Web Vitals or load times need improvement, when N+1 query patterns need fixing, or when profiling reveals bottlenecks.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
skills.description: Breaks work into ordered tasks. Use when you have a spec or clear requirements and need to break work into implementable tasks. Use when a task feels too large to start, when you need to estimate scope, or when parallel work is possible.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: pre-mortem
skills.description: Run a pre-mortem risk analysis on a PRD or launch plan. Categorizes risks as Tigers (real problems), Paper Tigers (overblown concerns), and Elephants (unspoken worries), then classifies as launch-blocking, fast-follow, or track. Use when preparing for launch, stress-testing a product plan, or identifying what could go wrong.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: pricing
skills.description: When the user wants to set pricing and packaging, or asks what to charge, whether to raise prices, or how to move existing customers: tiers, value metrics, per-seat vs usage, freemium and trials, willingness to pay, pricing pages. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls. For offers on services, courses, and high-ticket B2B, see offers.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: prioritization-frameworks
skills.description: Reference guide to 9 prioritization frameworks with formulas, when-to-use guidance, and templates — RICE, ICE, Kano, MoSCoW, Opportunity Score, and more. Use when selecting a prioritization method, comparing frameworks like RICE vs ICE, or learning how different prioritization approaches work.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: product-marketing
skills.description: When the user wants to create or update the product marketing context doc (.agents/product-marketing.md), or asks what belongs in it or whether positioning or ICP is clear enough: product, ICP, positioning, competitors, customer language, brand voice. Use it before other marketing skills on a new project, when the audience or positioning changes, and to log learnings.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: prompt-optimizer
skills.description: Creates, optimizes, and iteratively refines agent prompts, system prompts, developer prompts, and reusable prompt templates. Use when asked to improve a prompt, optimize a system prompt, rewrite an agent prompt, tune prompt wording, make a prompt more reliable, port prompts between OpenAI, Claude, or Gemini, or build prompt evals.
skills.authors: Functional Software, Inc. dba Sentry (Copyright 2025)

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: release-notes
skills.description: Generate user-facing release notes from tickets, PRDs, or changelogs. Creates clear, engaging summaries organized by category (new features, improvements, fixes). Use when writing release notes, creating changelogs, announcing product updates, or summarizing what shipped.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: requesting-code-review
skills.description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: retro
skills.description: Facilitate a structured sprint retrospective — what went well, what didn't, and prioritized action items with owners and deadlines. Use when running a retrospective, reflecting on a sprint, creating action items from team feedback, or learning how to run effective retros.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: security-and-hardening
skills.description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities. Use when auditing an input handler for vulnerabilities, when handling user input, authentication, data storage, or external integrations, or when checking a login flow is safe against the OWASP Top Ten. Use when building any feature that accepts untrusted data, manages user sessions or session cookies, or interacts with third-party services. Use when auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities, triaging package-manager audit findings, or assessing supply-chain risk in a new package. Use when personal data or privacy compliance (GDPR, CCPA) is involved.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: seo-audit
skills.description: When the user wants to audit or diagnose SEO, or asks why traffic dropped, a page won't rank, or whether a setup like canonicals, hreflang, or redirects is right: technical SEO, indexing, Google updates, on-page and titles, Core Web Vitals, local SEO. Start here when someone just says their SEO is bad. For pages at scale, see programmatic-seo. For structured data, see schema. For AI search, see ai-seo.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: shipping-and-launch
skills.description: Prepares production launches. Use when preparing to deploy to production, or when asking what needs to be in place before shipping. Use when you need a pre-launch checklist, when setting up monitoring, when planning a staged rollout, or when you need a rollback strategy.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC

skills.name: social
skills.description: When the user wants organic social content for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, or Facebook, or asks what to post, which format to favor, or from which account: posts, threads, carousels, short-form video scripts, calendars, build-in-public posts from commits, listening. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y' or broetry. For content strategy, see content-strategy. For paid ads, see ad-creative. For press, see public-relations.
skills.authors: Corey Haines and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Corey Haines)

skills.name: spec-driven-development
skills.description: Creates specs before coding. Use when starting a new project, feature, or significant change and no specification exists yet. Use when drafting a PRD or requirements document with objectives and scope, or when requirements are unclear, ambiguous, or only exist as a vague idea. Use when a single requirement spans several independently testable capabilities and needs decomposing into a capability map of modules before specifying. Use when evolving a shipped spec — scoping a V1, deferring ideas to a V2 backlog, or writing a follow-up spec for a change to an existing feature.
skills.authors: Addy Osmani and contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Addy Osmani)

skills.name: sql-queries
skills.description: Generate SQL queries from natural language descriptions. Supports BigQuery, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and other dialects. Reads database schemas from uploaded diagrams or documentation. Use when writing SQL, building data reports, exploring databases, or translating business questions into queries.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: stakeholder-map
skills.description: Build a stakeholder map using a power/interest grid, identify communication strategies per quadrant, and generate a communication plan. Use when managing stakeholders, preparing for a launch, aligning cross-functional teams, or planning stakeholder engagement.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: statistical-analysis
skills.description: Guided statistical analysis for research data - test selection, assumption checking, effect sizes, power analysis, Bayesian alternatives, and APA-formatted reporting. Use whenever a user wants to compare groups, test a hypothesis, analyze experimental or survey data, check statistical assumptions, compute required sample sizes, or write up results - even if they never name a specific test. Covers t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, correlation, regression, non-parametric and Bayesian methods. For low-level model APIs, see the statsmodels and pymc skills.
skills.authors: K-Dense Inc. (Copyright (c) 2025 K-Dense Inc.)

skills.name: summarize-interview
skills.description: Summarize a customer interview transcript into a structured template with JTBD, satisfaction signals, and action items. Use when processing interview recordings or transcripts, synthesizing discovery interviews, or creating interview summaries.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: summarize-meeting
skills.description: Summarize a meeting transcript into structured notes with date, participants, topic, key decisions, summary points, and action items. Use when processing meeting recordings, creating meeting notes, writing meeting minutes, or recapping discussions.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: survey-design
skills.description: Writing or reviewing a survey or questionnaire: customer feedback, NPS, CSAT, CES, pricing, market research, an in-app survey. Starts from the decision, asks about facts, pilots it, and reports the sample honestly.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: swot-analysis
skills.description: Perform a detailed SWOT analysis — strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats with actionable recommendations. Use when doing strategic assessment, competitive analysis, or evaluating a product or business position.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: theme-factory
skills.description: Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC

skills.name: user-personas
skills.description: Create refined user personas from research data — 3 personas with JTBD, pains, gains, and unexpected insights. Use when building personas from survey data, creating user profiles from research, or segmenting users for product decisions.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: user-stories
skills.description: Create user stories following the 3 C's (Card, Conversation, Confirmation) and INVEST criteria with descriptions, design links, and acceptance criteria. Use when writing user stories, breaking down features into backlog items, or defining acceptance criteria.
skills.authors: Pawel Huryn and contributors (Copyright (c) 2026 Pawel Huryn)

skills.name: using-git-worktrees
skills.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
skills.authors: Jesse Vincent and Superpowers contributors (Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse Vincent)

skills.name: webapp-testing
skills.description: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.
skills.authors: Anthropic, PBC
